title: Proposal: extend `window.open()` to split tabs, and add declarative equivalents for `window.open()` generally
body: ### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? {See https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9644 for a prior *very* similar proposal. This issue intends to supersede that issue, and is quite similar. I debated just commenting there, but I don't want there to be confusion about the specifics of the API shape being proposed.} Many browsers these days include a "split tabs" feature, where two separate top level URLs can be viewed side-by-side within a single "tab" of the browser. However, there is no way to request for `window.open()` to open the new URL in this mode. Neither is there a way to cause a link-click to open in this mode. Please see the explainer for all the details: https://github.com/mfreed7/split-tabs But TL;DR, the proposal for the imperative API is a new `"split"` [window features](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#window-feature-is-set) token: ``` // Basic: request a split tab. window.open("https://www.example.com", "_blank", "split"); // Open on the left, taking 30% of the width. window.open("https://www.example.com", "_blank", "split,splitposition=left,splitsize=30"); ``` and the declarative API is a new `windowFeatures` attribute: ``` Open in a split tab ``` Note that the declarative proposal also allows links to open popups, which wasn't possible before without JS. This has been prototyped in Chromium, which you can try out using the latest Canary build, plus `--enable-features="WindowOpenSplitTab"` on the command line. (And soon by just enabling Experimental Web Platform Features instead.) Draft spec PR: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13245 Thoughts appreciated!
